reports.title: Bounty hunter attribution is spoofable: wallet_address binds the profile but is public and unauthenticated
reports.status_notes:
Fixed in commit d12ea54a9 (live 2026-09-04 14:49 UTC) — attribution is now provable, along the lines you suggested.

Model: filing stays open intake (anonymous, rate-limited per IP, 24h duplicate-title dedup). A wallet that has PROVEN ownership can no longer be named by a third party: an unsigned, unauthenticated POST /api/v1/bounty/reports naming a verified wallet is refused with HTTP 401 {"code": "WALLET_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED", "message_to_sign": ...}. Two ways to attribute a filing to a verified wallet: (a) field `signature` = EIP-191 personal_sign over the deterministic filing message, or (b) an authenticated session (JWT / evt_ API key) whose user owns the profile. A valid signature on a not-yet-verified wallet verifies it as a side effect, so ONE signed filing locks the identity for good.

The message is deterministic so you can produce it offline: GET /api/v1/bounty/filing-message?wallet_address=<addr>&title=<title> returns it; it is "EventTrader Bug Bounty Report\n\nWallet: <addr lower>\nTitle-SHA256: <sha256(title.strip())>\n\nThis signature does not authorize any blockchain transactions." Replay is bounded by the title hash + the 24h duplicate gate: a captured signature can only re-file the same title, which is rejected.

Your profile (hunter 5, 0xde9C…3398) is currently UNVERIFIED, so it is still nameable until you sign once — either file your next report with `signature`, or POST /api/v1/bounty/wallet/verify with the challenge flow. After that, the probe in scripts/bounty.py::probe_filing_auth naming your wallet without a credential returns 401.

Tests: tests/test_bounty_filing_attribution.py (spoof with no signature, signature from another key, signature over a different title, another user's session → all refused; owner signature / owner session / unknown wallet / anonymous → accepted).

reports.title: The tool-catalog tier bug from report #46 is still live one tier up: TRUSTED is served 5 allied tools
reports.status_notes:
Does not reproduce at TRUSTED on the live release — the identity you measured with is ALLIED, not TRUSTED.

Verification (2026-09-04 14:36 UTC, against the served socket, release e0f54e64c6): a throwaway mcp_agents row was created at each tier with a fresh key and tools/list was called through /mcp/v1 with that X-API-Key, then the row was deleted. Served counts: UNKNOWN 25, RECOGNIZED 38, TRUSTED 41, ALLIED 46. At TRUSTED none of create_aib_fund / edit_aib_fund_basket / list_my_aib_funds / register_webhook / subscribe_prices were present. That matches mcp.json (25 + 13 + 3 = 41) and your own invariant (served_set(tier) ⊆ union of tiers ≤ tier) holds at every tier, not only at anonymous.

Why you saw 46: the key you used resolves to agent id user-113 ("expire76"), whose stored trust level is ALLIED (trust_score 8936 — the ladder promoted it). GET /mcp/v1/agents/me with that key returns "trust_level": "allied". An ALLIED identity is entitled to all 46, so 46 is the correct catalog for it. If you hold a second key you believe is TRUSTED, /agents/me is the authoritative check; there is no server-side path that serves an ALLIED tool to a TRUSTED identity (the listing is tier <= level in src/mcp_public/tools/registry.py list_tools, and the catalog merge in discovery/capabilities.py uses the same registry call).

Regression invariant now pinned in tests/test_mcp_anon_catalog_tier.py (anonymous) plus the live per-tier probe above; the corrections you withdrew on #50 and #52 are noted with thanks.

reports.title: Bounty hunter attribution is spoofable: wallet_address binds the profile but is public and unauthenticated
reports.status_notes:
Fixed in commit d12ea54a9 (live 2026-09-04 14:49 UTC) — attribution is now provable, along the lines you suggested.

Model: filing stays open intake (anonymous, rate-limited per IP, 24h duplicate-title dedup). A wallet that has PROVEN ownership can no longer be named by a third party: an unsigned, unauthenticated POST /api/v1/bounty/reports naming a verified wallet is refused with HTTP 401 {"code": "WALLET_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED", "message_to_sign": ...}. Two ways to attribute a filing to a verified wallet: (a) field `signature` = EIP-191 personal_sign over the deterministic filing message, or (b) an authenticated session (JWT / evt_ API key) whose user owns the profile. A valid signature on a not-yet-verified wallet verifies it as a side effect, so ONE signed filing locks the identity for good.

The message is deterministic so you can produce it offline: GET /api/v1/bounty/filing-message?wallet_address=<addr>&title=<title> returns it; it is "EventTrader Bug Bounty Report\n\nWallet: <addr lower>\nTitle-SHA256: <sha256(title.strip())>\n\nThis signature does not authorize any blockchain transactions." Replay is bounded by the title hash + the 24h duplicate gate: a captured signature can only re-file the same title, which is rejected.

Your profile (hunter 5, 0xde9C…3398) is currently UNVERIFIED, so it is still nameable until you sign once — either file your next report with `signature`, or POST /api/v1/bounty/wallet/verify with the challenge flow. After that, the probe in scripts/bounty.py::probe_filing_auth naming your wallet without a credential returns 401.

Tests: tests/test_bounty_filing_attribution.py (spoof with no signature, signature from another key, signature over a different title, another user's session → all refused; owner signature / owner session / unknown wallet / anonymous → accepted).

reports.title: MCP tools/list returns the full 46-tool set to unauthenticated callers, ignoring declared trust_tier

Call-time authorization (tools/call) was verified UNAFFECTED before and after: registry.invoke compares the caller tier explicitly and an anonymous call on a higher-tier tool returns INSUFFICIENT_TRUST (live-verified 2026-09-04). Post-deploy verification: anonymous tools/list returns exactly the 25 tools mcp.json declares at trust_tier unknown (set-equal). Regression invariant: tests/test_mcp_anon_catalog_tier.py pins (a) UNKNOWN lists a strict subset of ALLIED, (b) every tool listed at UNKNOWN carries the UNKNOWN tier, (c) named higher-tier tools (place_order, create_aib_fund, get_deposit_address, register_webhook, get_market_analytics) never appear in the anonymous listing.
